acceptance: A local spike with the pinned omp Linux reviewer in a container and the gateway on the host records checks A-F with labelled REAL/SYNTHETIC evidence and a GO/NO-GO verdict.
Every fallback-chain provider completes a request through the gateway, or the gap is reported before any cutover.

After an owner GO: a cutover PR forwards only OMP_GATEWAY_TOKEN to the reviewer, writes a minimal role map and a gateway models.yml, and updates the docs to claim no file confinement; it passes review and merges.
A hosted oracle run completes through the gateway, after which the owner deletes the old reviewer secrets and rotates the broker token, API keys and Claude setup token.
description:
The reviewer process holds the Claude OAuth token, the OpenAI, Meta and Gemini keys and the broker token (oracle-verdict.yml attempt jobs), and a broker client receives OAuth access tokens and API keys for the whole vault (omp auth-broker-gateway.md). The model can read files outside the checkout, so any read path exposes all of them.

Owner decision 2026-10-22: the --trusted-extension tool_call guard is rejected. An adversarial review found that it covers only tool arguments and misses prompt @ mentions, context-file imports and in-process cfg://. It also leaves every credential in the process, copies omp's private path grammar, and its required --help check cannot pass on the pinned build. Its uncommitted prototype and worktree were deleted.

Approved direction (D1), prototype only for now: the reviewer gets only an `omp auth-gateway serve` client token, scoped by `models`/`accounts` to the role primaries and the fallback-chain models. The owner keeps the fallbacks. The reviewer's models.yml points each provider at the gateway, and a minimal role map replaces the full OMP_AGENT_CONFIG. Provider keys and the broker token leave the runner.

Independent hardening ships separately: fetch.enabled false, context-file discovery providers disabled, prompt @ path mentions neutralized, and Dispute: replies limited to OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR.
